title: Missing Semicolon
explanation: Java statements must be terminated with a semicolon ';'. The compiler encountered the next token before this statement was completed.
cause: A statement (such as a variable declaration, assignment, or method call) is missing the terminating semicolon.
solution: Add a semicolon ';' at the end of the statement line.

title: Unbalanced Parentheses
explanation: Every opening parenthesis '(' in Java must have a matching closing parenthesis ')'.
cause: A method invocation, condition, or mathematical expression is missing a closing or opening parenthesis.
solution: Check parentheses balance and add the missing closing or opening parenthesis.

pattern: '\}' expected|'\{' expected|reached end of file while parsing
title: Unbalanced Curly Braces
explanation: Java uses curly braces '{' and '}' to define code blocks for classes, methods, and control flow structures.
cause: A class or method body has an unclosed block or extra curly brace.
solution: Ensure every '{' has a matching '}' and check block indentation.

title: Unclosed String / Character Literal
explanation: String literals in Java must be enclosed within double quotation marks "...".
cause: A string literal begins with a quote but lacks the closing quote on the same line.
solution: Add the closing quote before the end of the line.

title: Cannot Find Symbol
explanation: The compiler cannot recognize the variable, method, or class name you referenced.
cause: Possible causes: (1) Typo in the name, (2) Variable not declared, (3) Variable is outside current scope, or (4) Missing import statement.
solution: Verify spelling, declare the variable with its data type before use, or import the required class.

title: Incompatible Types
explanation: Java is strongly typed: a value of one type cannot be assigned to an incompatible variable without explicit casting or conversion.
cause: Attempting to assign a value (e.g. String) to a variable of a different type (e.g. int).
solution: Change the variable type to match the value, or convert the value explicitly (e.g., Integer.parseInt()).

pattern: variable .* might not have been initialized
title: Uninitialized Variable
explanation: Local variables in Java are not given default values and must be initialized before being read.
cause: Reading a local variable before assigning an initial value to it.
solution: Assign a default or initial value when declaring the variable (e.g., int x = 0;).

pattern: non-static .* cannot be referenced from a static context
title: Non-Static Reference From Static Context
explanation: A static method (like main) belongs to the class itself, while instance variables and methods belong to specific object instances.
cause: Calling an instance method or accessing an instance field directly from a static method.
solution: Either make the referenced member 'static', or instantiate an object of the class first.

title: Missing Return Statement
explanation: A method with a non-void return type must return a value along all possible execution paths.
cause: Execution can exit the method without hitting a 'return' statement.
solution: Add a return statement at the end of the method or handle all branch cases.

title: Unreachable Statement
explanation: The compiler detected code that can never be executed under any circumstance.
cause: Statements placed immediately after a 'return', 'break', 'continue', or infinite loop.
solution: Move or remove code placed after unconditional jump or return statements.

title: Arithmetic Exception: Division by Zero
explanation: In Java integer arithmetic, dividing any integer by zero triggers an ArithmeticException.
cause: The divisor in a '/' or '%' operation evaluated to 0 at runtime.
solution: Check that the denominator is not zero before performing division.

title: Array Index Out of Bounds
explanation: Java arrays are 0-indexed. Accessing an index < 0 or >= array.length causes an exception.
cause: Loop condition allowed index to reach array.length (off-by-one) or negative index.
solution: Ensure loop condition uses 'i < array.length' instead of '<='.

title: Missing Colon ':'
explanation: In Python, compound statements introducing a block (if, for, while, def, class, etc.) must end with a colon ':'.
cause: The header line of an if, for, while, def, or class statement is missing a trailing colon.
solution: Add ':' at the end of the compound statement line.

pattern: '\(' was never closed|closing parenthesis .* does not match
title: Unclosed Parenthesis
explanation: Python requires balanced parentheses '()', square brackets '[]', and curly braces '{}'.
cause: A function call, tuple, or expression opened a parenthesis that was never closed.
solution: Add the matching closing parenthesis ')' at the end of the expression.

pattern: IndentationError: expected an indented block|IndentationError: unexpected indent
title: Indentation Error
explanation: Python uses indentation (whitespace) instead of braces to define code blocks and scope.
cause: Code inside a block is not properly indented, or indentation is inconsistent.
solution: Use 4 spaces per indentation level. Ensure the code block is indented under its header.

title: Name Not Defined
explanation: Python encountered a variable or function name that has not been defined in the current scope.
cause: Possible typo, or using a variable before assigning a value to it, or forgetting to import a module.
solution: Check spelling, assign the variable prior to reading it, or import the required module.

pattern: TypeError: unsupported operand type|TypeError: can only concatenate
title: Type Error
explanation: An operation or function was applied to an object of an inappropriate or mismatched type.
cause: Attempting to perform arithmetic between incompatible types, such as adding a string and an integer.
solution: Convert the types explicitly using int(), str(), or float() before operating.

title: Division by Zero
explanation: In Python, dividing a number by 0 or 0.0 raises a ZeroDivisionError.
cause: The second operand of a '/', '//', or '%' operator evaluated to 0.
solution: Check that the divisor is not zero before dividing (e.g., if b != 0: ...).

pattern: IndexError: list index out of range
title: List Index Out of Range
explanation: Attempted to access an index that is outside the bounds of the list.
cause: Accessing list[i] where i >= len(list) or i < -len(list).
solution: Verify list length using len(list) or iterate using 'for item in my_list:'.
